messages:
maria-cs: FYI — a handful of onboarding customers reported degraded relevance for embeddings and a few 502s during bulk ingest after the overnight model ops change. tagging eng + sre; a couple of these are mid-renewal trials so looking to coordinate comms.

jon-eng: investigating. signs point to batched ingest path hitting a memory growth with new quantized model. reproducing on staging with same batch size.

taylor-sre: opening incident INC-2025-089. setting severity to medium-high while we scope blast radius. mitigation options: temporarily throttle ingest batches or revert model artifact. applying throttling now to reduce errors.

csbot: Incident INC-2025-089 created by taylor-sre | status: investigating | link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-089

maria-cs: thanks. need a short comm for affected contacts: one-line impact, current mitigation, ETA for full fix, statement about data, and any goodwill offered. keep it brief for account teams.

jon-eng: draft technical note for CS: "Cause: memory leak in quantized model's batched decode path causing intermittent 502s during high-volume bulk ingest. Mitigation: temporary batch throttling rolled out to affected clusters; working on a rebuilt artifact to eliminate leak. ETA for artifact and validation ~24-36 hours if tests pass; rollback possible sooner if needed."

kevin-legal: okay on wording about data exposure? we should explicitly say "no customer data loss or exfiltration detected" rather than "no data exposed". also don't promise exact hours beyond 72.

maria-cs: updated customer-friendly draft below — will send to the 8 impacted onboarding contacts after signoff.

maria-cs: ```Hi <Customer Contact>,

Wewanted to let you know we observed reduced relevance for embedding results and intermittent 502 errors for high-volume bulk ingest requests after a runtime update deployed last night. Our engineers have identified a memory-growth issue in the model artifact and have applied temporary throttling to affected ingest pipelines while we validate a rebuilt artifact.

We do not detect any customer data loss or exfiltration. We expect to have a validated artifact and broader mitigation in place within 72 hours; we will update you sooner if we rollback or complete the fix earlier.

As a gesture for the disruption, we will apply a small account credit to impacted onboarding usage and prioritize a technical review call to help tune ingest parameters for your workload.

Reply to this message if you would like to schedule the review call.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Support```

taylor-sre: good. please also add a portal status line: "temporary throttling applied; artifact rebuild in progress; monitoring request success and relevance metrics".

maria-cs: will post to portal after we confirm the throttle is stable for 60m. tagging renewals for the top 3 trials so they can reach out proactively. @jon-eng can you drop a short timeline graph for those accounts?

jon-eng: prepping error-rate + relevance delta charts now; will DM direct links.

kevin-legal: retention note: save copies of outbound emails for compliance. cs team, please keep a record in the incident drive.

maria-cs: copy that. plan recap: 1) throttle in place 2) portal status posted 3) targeted emails to 8 onboarding contacts 4) credits + priority review calls offered 5) RCA within 72 hours with root cause and long-term fix ETA.

jon-eng: also adding an e2e regression test to catch memory growth on large-batch ingests. filing PR after artifact validation.

maria-cs: thanks all. please ping when portal post is live and when the 60m stability window completes. well collect feedback from the onboarding leads and add to the renewal risk tracker. :thumbsup:
